text:
Have Athena reconsider its own design every five finished tasks, and record whether it is settling. Sri, 2026-10-17: "Let's also have Athena reconsider its own design every few jobs to see if we arrive at a stable design" and "I'm not sold the API surface should be considered settled". This builds on the design-surface inventory and diff (the previous job).
Plan: (1) Add a design-reviewer role in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs beside the steward, with a fixed prompt and cadence_tasks = 5, run by the same tick mechanism as the steward (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs). (2) Each review reads docs/architecture.md, the design docs, the surface diff since the last review, and the job and intervention records since then, and writes docs/design/reviews/design-review-<n>.md with: what changed; proposed structural changes, each with its evidence and the rung it touches; a section on the API surface saying which commands, config sections or record schemas to merge, rename or drop, and why; and the stability counts. (3) Stability is recorded per review: the surface changes since the last review (from the diff, computed by code) and the number of structural changes the review proposes. A design is settling when both fall across reviews. (4) Proposals at or below the role's highest rung are queued as requests, as the steward's are; proposals above it wait for Sri.
Acceptance:
- cargo test: the role validates; with a fake driver, the design reviewer runs after five finished tasks and not before, and writes one review file and one record.
- cargo test: the review record holds the surface-diff counts computed by code, not by the model (a test changes the model's output and the counts stay the same).
- cargo test: a proposal above the role's rung is listed as waiting for a person, not queued as work.
- athena status shows the latest review's stability counts beside the previous review's.
- clippy with -D warnings and fmt --check are clean; CHANGELOG.md has an entry; docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md has a section on the role.
Out of scope: acting on the proposals, and changing the steward.
